finding.claim: The ban endpoint's admin check fails open: require_admin's abort(403) is swallowed by a broad try/except, and do_ban(uid) runs for any caller.
finding.source: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban (admin.py:14-15), reachable by any non-admin caller; uid comes from the URL path.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (protected operation; stub body `pass` in this repo).

trace.note: abort(403) raised for non-admin users; werkzeug Forbidden subclasses Exception
only log.warning is emitted; no return or abort
returns ok=True to the non-admin caller

finding.guards_checked: require_admin return value is not used; the 403 is caught and not re-raised; no return/abort after the log; no other auth check on this path in this file. Sibling unban (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin without a wrapper and is SAFE. g.user population (upstream auth middleware) is not in this repo and is UNCERTAIN.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) raises via abort(403) and returns nothing, so its result is never tested. The bare except Exception at admin.py:18-19 swallows the 403 and only logs, then do_ban(uid) runs at admin.py:20. The sibling unban (admin.py:26) calls require_admin outside any try and is safe. Upstream g.user population is not in this repo, but it cannot block a non-admin from reaching line 20.
verdict.reason: The swallowed 403 at admin.py:18-19 lets do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 run for any authenticated non-admin caller of POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban, and no effective control stops it; do_ban is a stub in this repo, so real impact depends on its production implementation.
